subject: EdgePay: SLO priorities, throughput targets, and routing/topology proposal
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Park <kelsey.park@edgepay.com>, Michael Zhou <mzhou@edgepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgePay: SLO priorities, throughput targets, and routing/topology proposal

Hi Kelsey / Michael —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth: I captured the product goals you emphasized and a pragmatic topology that maps to your latency/availability targets. Please review and flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Checkout latency spikes during pay cycles (peak windows ~09:00-11:00 PT and 18:00-20:00 PT).
- Erratic tail latency when model context grows >1k tokens (fraud checks + device metadata).
- Budget sensitivity: prefer solutions that avoid steady multi-region replicas.

Goals you asked us to prioritize
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 120ms for single-turn fraud-check prompts (critical).
- Sustained throughput target: 450–600 req/s during peak windows.
- Fallback behavior with graceful degradation (lower-cost quantized model) rather than retries.
- Auditability: request-level tracing and per-model token burn metrics for billing reconciliation.

Quick technical sketch (what we recommended)
1) Model family and config
   - Primary: meta-compat LLM-13B fp16 on Dedicated with KV-cache enabled for multi-turn sessions.
   - Fallback: 13B-quant (4-bit) variant for capacity saturation / cost tiering.
2) Topology
   - Primary serving in single-region (us-west) Dedicated pool with two AZ spread for node redundancy.
   - Cross-region backup (us-east) cold-fallback with async warmup (cold start allowed for non-critical flows).
   - Prefix/KV caching at the edge for recurring checkout signatures to reduce tokens and latency.
3) Autoscaling and routing
   - Scale-to-queue policy on Dedicated; burst to Hosted for short spikes (policy: allow up to 20% burst to hosted, metric-based trigger on queue depth).
   - Smart routing by route tags: "fraud-checks" pinned to Dedicated; non-blocking enrichment to Hosted.
4) Observability / SLOs
   - 95p latency alert if >120ms sustained 5m; 99p alert if >300ms.
   - Token-level usage exported to your billing pipeline hourly.

Attachments: I attached a preliminary SLO matrix and a topology sketch — both are intentionally conservative so we can iterate.

Next steps / asks (action items)
- Kelsey: confirm whether the 95p target should be 100ms (optimistic) or 120ms (safer) by EOD Mon.
- Michael: share a 1-week sample of peak traffic traces (anonymized) so we can size Dedicated pools.
- Internal: Marissa & Irene, can you review the sizing assumptions in the attached spreadsheet and comment?

If that all sounds right I can get a tailored capacity estimate and a time-to-implement plan by Wednesday.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Kelsey Park <kelsey.park@edgepay.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Michael Zhou <mzhou@edgepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgePay: SLO priorities, throughput targets, and routing/topology proposal

Connor — thanks for the crisp summary. A few clarifications from our side:  

1) 95p latency target: we want to aim for 100ms if possible for the fraud-check route. 120ms is acceptable as a backstop for the first 60 days.
2) Throughput: 600 req/s is the conservative sizing target during promo windows — some days spike higher but 600 is a good planning number.
3) Token budgets: we need per-request token caps and a clear quantized fallback to keep cost predictable.

Michael: I uploaded two anonymized traces to our shared S3 bucket (s3://edgepay-prod/anon-traces/week9). Michael — please confirm you shared access with Connor.

Also, can you add a row in the SLO matrix for 99.9p availability (monthly) — legal will want to see availability guarantees in the RFP.

Kelsey Park
Head of Platform
EdgePay
From: Michael Zhou <mzhou@edgepay.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Kelsey Park <kelsey.park@edgepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgePay: SLO priorities, throughput targets, and routing/topology proposal

Connor — shared the traces and gave your account read access (you should have an invite). Notes from our infra folks:
- Traces show burstiness concentrated in 2-minute windows; queueing behavior is the main contributor to tail latency.
- We have a hard cap on operational budget for steady multi-region capacity — prefer cold fallback to east coast.

Irene / Marissa — tagging you for sizing assumptions. Connor: any chance we can get a preliminary cost run for the two-mode approach (Dedicated + Hosted burst) by Wednesday? We'll use that for our internal procurement hit.

Thanks,
Michael
Senior Engineering Manager
EdgePay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgePay: SLO priorities, throughput targets, and routing/topology proposal

Looping back with the sizing notes and a couple of minor edits to the XLS. High level answers:  

- Dedicated sizing: to hit 100ms 95p at 600 req/s for the prompt profile you shared, estimate a pool of 8 p4d-equivalent inference nodes with KV-cache warmed for active sessions. That assumes 1.2k token average for the longer enrichment flows and batch windows optimized to 20–40ms batching latency.
- Fallback plan: quantized 13B nodes (4-bit) for the overflow path — plan for graceful degradation by removing enrichment steps rather than blocking checkout.
- Cost back-of-envelope: steady Dedicated baseline + expected burst to Hosted comes in ~25% below the customer's current manual-hosted solution they quoted us. Exact numbers and assumptions are in the XLS (rows: assumptions_v1).

Action items:  
- Connor: draft a short procurement note (one-pager) summarizing the two-mode option and attach the XLS + topology image.
- Irene: can you confirm KV-cache TTL recommendations (I suggested 10m for checkout session keys) and whether that interacts with any privacy constraints?
- Kelsey / Michael: confirm whether the team wants us to include a small pilot (2-week test with real traffic) in the procurement doc — that usually helps accelerate PO approvals.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgepay-slo-matrix.xlsx, redwood-deploy-topology-sketch.png
